output.title: Decreasing students’ stress through time management training

scenes.narration: University students often feel stressed, and this paper asks whether a short time management training can change that experience for undergraduates.
scenes.layout_description: A student sits at a desk with scattered papers and a small clock, while an orange arrow points toward a calmer notebook.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist hand-drawn black ink line art on cream background, a stressed undergraduate at a cluttered desk with a clock, orange and yellow highlights around the clock and papers, lots of white space.

scenes.narration: The authors studied twenty-three undergraduate students who completed a training and reported demands, perceived stress, and perceived control of time before and after it.
scenes.layout_description: Three simple icons—clipboard, stress wave, and clock—sit in a row beside a small group of students.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn line art of a small group of students with three floating icons: clipboard, wavy stress lines, and a clock, highlighted with orange circles.

scenes.narration: They used a non-equivalent dependent variable design, meaning demands served as a control variable that should not change if the training worked.
scenes.layout_description: Two paths are shown, one for stress and control of time, and one for demands, with the demands path staying flat.
scenes.visual_prompt: A simple diagram with two rising arrows for stress and control of time, and one flat line labeled demands, all in black ink with orange accents.

scenes.narration: The training was expected to increase perceived control of time and decrease perceived stress, while demands should remain unchanged after training.
scenes.layout_description: A student stands between an upward clock icon and a downward stress icon, while a separate demand icon stays still.
scenes.visual_prompt: Student figure between a clock with upward arrow and a stress cloud with downward arrow, plus a separate unmoving stack of tasks, minimalist line art.

scenes.narration: The intervention focused on prioritizing, goal setting, strategy development, daily planning, and monitoring, all meant to help students manage time better.
scenes.layout_description: Five small symbols form a simple sequence around a central student notebook.
scenes.visual_prompt: A notebook with five surrounding icons: star for priorities, target for goals, stepping stones for strategy, calendar for planning, and check marks for monitoring, in black ink with orange highlights.

scenes.narration: Students first reflected on their activities, then set concrete goals, planned steps, anticipated obstacles, scheduled their day, and checked task completion.
scenes.layout_description: A left-to-right storyboard shows a student moving from reflection to planning to checking off tasks.
scenes.visual_prompt: A sequence of four small panels: thinking student, target with deadline, calendar schedule, and checklist with ticks, minimalist line art with yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: The sample came from a medium-sized German university, with students from all faculties invited as an extracurricular activity and no incentives offered.
scenes.layout_description: A university building sits behind a small invitation board and a group of diverse students.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple campus building, invitation board, and a mixed group of students approaching, drawn in black ink with orange arrows pointing to the invitation board.

scenes.narration: The training lasted 4 h, and questionnaires were completed directly before training, then 2 weeks later, and again 4 weeks later.
scenes.layout_description: A timeline runs across the slide with three marked points and a small training block at the start.
scenes.visual_prompt: A clean horizontal timeline with a training box at the beginning and three dots labeled by hand, with orange and yellow highlights on the measurement points.

scenes.narration: Although forty-eight students began, only twenty-three completed all questionnaires, and those twenty-three were used for the main analyses.
scenes.layout_description: A larger group narrows down to a smaller group, with the final group highlighted.
scenes.visual_prompt: A funnel-like drawing of students shrinking from a larger cluster to a smaller cluster of 23, with orange highlight around the final group.

scenes.narration: The final group had a mean age of 23.30 years, and 52 % were female; they studied several different subjects and mostly had little experience with time management.
scenes.layout_description: A small circle of students is surrounded by subject labels and a simple experience meter.
scenes.visual_prompt: A group of students with a small age tag, a female symbol highlighted in orange, and a low-to-mid experience meter, all in sketch style.

scenes.narration: Before training, most students reported no or little experience with time management strategies, which the authors thought might make training especially useful.
scenes.layout_description: A simple bar chart shows most responses in the low-experience categories.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn bar chart with tallest bars at no experience and little experience, orange highlight on those bars, minimalist cream background.

scenes.narration: Time management behaviour was measured with 18 items, perceived stress with the tension scale, perceived control of time with 10 items, and demands with 5 items.
scenes.layout_description: Four measurement cards are arranged neatly, each with a small icon and item count.
scenes.visual_prompt: Four cards or sheets labeled by hand with tiny icons: checklist, stress wave, clock, and workload stack, with orange circles around the item counts.

scenes.narration: In the results, the use of taught time management strategies increased significantly from before training to 4 weeks after, and nearly significantly after 2 weeks.
scenes.layout_description: An upward line for strategy use rises across the three time points, with the middle point marked as nearly significant.
scenes.visual_prompt: A simple upward trend line with three dots, the last dot highest, and a small orange question mark near the middle point to suggest nearly significant.

scenes.narration: For the first comparison, the overall time effect was significant, and perceived stress showed a significant decrease 2 weeks after training.
scenes.layout_description: Two side-by-side panels compare pretest and 2-week posttest, with the stress symbol shrinking.
scenes.visual_prompt: Before-and-after sketch: a stressed student on the left and a calmer student on the right, with an orange downward arrow between them and a small stats note icon.

scenes.narration: Perceived control of time showed only a tendency at 2 weeks, so the change was in the expected direction but not yet significant.
scenes.layout_description: A clock icon moves slightly upward, but the arrow is faint and marked as tentative.
scenes.visual_prompt: A clock with a small upward arrow and a dotted outline, suggesting a tentative rise, with orange used sparingly to mark the trend.

scenes.narration: By 4 weeks after training, the overall time effect was significant again, and both perceived stress and perceived control of time changed significantly.
scenes.layout_description: A three-point timeline ends with two strong arrows, one down for stress and one up for control.
scenes.visual_prompt: Timeline ending in two bold arrows: stress cloud down and clock up, both highlighted in orange and yellow, clean line art.

scenes.narration: The paper says the training effect was much stronger for students with no or little experience than for those with moderate or some experience.
scenes.layout_description: Two small student groups are compared side by side, with the less experienced group surrounded by larger arrows.
scenes.visual_prompt: Split scene with two groups of students; the left group has bigger orange arrows around them, the right group smaller arrows, showing stronger effect for the left.

scenes.narration: For demands, the control variable, there were no significant changes at 2 weeks or at 4 weeks after training.
scenes.layout_description: A workload stack stays level across the timeline while the other measures move.
scenes.visual_prompt: A flat line with a stack of papers or duties sitting unchanged above it, orange highlight only on the unchanged line.

scenes.narration: The authors interpret this pattern as evidence that the training reduced perceived stress and increased perceived control of time, rather than just producing a placebo effect.
scenes.layout_description: A central training box points to stress and control outcomes, while a faded placebo bubble is pushed aside.
scenes.visual_prompt: Training box with arrows to a smaller stress cloud and larger clock, and a faint crossed-out placebo bubble, minimalist black ink with orange accents.

scenes.narration: They also argue that prioritizing, goal setting, daily planning, and monitoring may have given students more orientation in their studies.
scenes.layout_description: A student follows a path made of small planning symbols toward a clear goal flag.
scenes.visual_prompt: A student walking along stepping stones labeled with tiny symbols toward a flag, with orange highlights on the path and goal.

scenes.narration: The authors note that the intervention was short, only 4 h, yet it still had a positive impact in this mixed student sample.
scenes.layout_description: A small training block sits beside a group of students from different fields, showing a compact but effective intervention.
scenes.visual_prompt: A compact 4 h training box next to a diverse student group, with a small orange burst indicating positive impact.

scenes.narration: They also say students with little experience may profit more, and they recommend further studies with larger samples to strengthen conclusions.
scenes.layout_description: A small sample icon grows into a larger one, with a note asking for more studies.
scenes.visual_prompt: A small cluster of students beside a larger empty outline of a future sample, with an orange arrow expanding outward.

scenes.narration: The authors mention that about half the students left before the second measurement, and they compare this dropout with other intervention studies.
scenes.layout_description: A group of students splits, with many walking away before the next checkpoint.
scenes.visual_prompt: A line of students moving toward a second checkpoint, with roughly half fading out before it, using orange to mark the checkpoint.

scenes.narration: They suggest future work should compare time management training with other stress-reducing interventions and test whether effects last longer.
scenes.layout_description: Several different intervention paths branch from one starting point and continue into the distance.
scenes.visual_prompt: A branching path diagram from one student to several labeled intervention boxes, with orange arrows extending forward to show future comparison.

scenes.narration: The paper also points to possible performance outcomes, but says experimental studies are still needed to examine causal effects in higher education.
scenes.layout_description: A student with a grade sheet stands beside a question mark and a research beaker icon.
scenes.visual_prompt: Student holding a paper with a simple upward performance arrow, next to a question mark and small experiment symbols, line art only.

scenes.narration: Their practical takeaway is simple: prioritize tasks, set clear goals, plan the work day, and monitor progress to help students manage stress.
scenes.layout_description: A final checklist fills the center of the slide, framed by a calm student and a clock.
scenes.visual_prompt: A clean checklist with four hand-drawn check marks, a calm student beside it, and a small clock highlighted in orange.

scenes.narration: Overall, this study suggests time management training may help undergraduate well-being, but the authors stress that more student studies are still needed.
scenes.layout_description: The closing slide shows a student beside a clock and a small open path forward.
scenes.visual_prompt: A calm student standing next to a clock and an open road leading forward, with orange and yellow highlights suggesting cautious optimism.
